about: White to yellow belt grading content. Learn, Quiz and Ask all read this file. Official ITF wording is copied character for character from the sources named on each quote.
gradingScope: ITF Taekwon-Do only. Grading 1 = 10th to 9th kup. Grading 2 = 9th to 8th kup.

items.title: What the word Taekwon-Do means
items.english: Tae is foot, Kwon is fist or hand, Do is the way
items.simple: Tae means foot (kicking). Kwon means fist or hand (punching). Do means the way.
items.learnBody: Taekwon-Do is made of three little words. Tae means foot (kicking). Kwon means fist or hand (punching). Do means the way, like a way of living and learning.
items.quiz: What do the three parts of the word Taekwon-Do mean?
items.answer: Tae is foot, Kwon is fist or hand, Do is the way.
wrong: Tae is hand, Kwon is foot, Do is the belt.
Tae is jump, Kwon is kick, Do is the dojang.
items.why: Tae means foot (kicking). Kwon means fist or hand (punching). Do means the way.

items.title: Who started Taekwon-Do
items.simple: The founder of Taekwon-Do is General Choi Hong Hi. He was a general in the Korean army. He was born in 1918 and died in 2002.
items.learnBody: The founder of Taekwon-Do is General Choi Hong Hi. He was a general in the Korean army. He was born in 1918 and died in 2002.
items.quiz: Who is the founder of Taekwon-Do?

items.title: When Taekwon-Do got its name
items.simple: General Choi gave Taekwon-Do its name on 11 April 1955. You can think of 11 April as Taekwon-Do's name day.
items.learnBody: General Choi gave Taekwon-Do its name on 11 April 1955. You can think of 11 April as Taekwon-Do's name day.
items.quiz: In which year was Taekwon-Do given its name?

items.title: What ITF means
items.simple: ITF stands for International Taekwon-Do Federation. General Choi started it in Seoul, Korea, on 22 March 1966. Our club does ITF Taekwon-Do. World Taekwondo (WT) is a different style with different patterns, so this app only covers ITF.
items.learnBody: ITF stands for International Taekwon-Do Federation. General Choi started it in Seoul, Korea, on 22 March 1966. Our club does ITF Taekwon-Do. World Taekwondo (WT) is a different style with different patterns, so this app only covers ITF.
items.quiz: What do the letters ITF stand for?

items.title: What the white belt means
items.english: Innocence, as that of a beginning student who has no previous knowledge of Taekwon-Do

official.text: White signifies innocence, as that of a beginning student who has no previous knowledge of Taekwon-Do.

items.simple: everyone starts with a white belt. You are a beginner, just starting to learn, with lots to learn.
items.quiz: What does the white belt mean?
items.answer: Innocence, as that of a beginning student who has no previous knowledge of Taekwon-Do.
wrong: Danger, cautioning the student to exercise control and warning the opponent to stay away.
The plant's growth as the Taekwon-Do skill begins to develop.
items.why: In simple words: everyone starts with a white belt. You are a beginner, just starting to learn.

items.title: The five tenets
items.english: Courtesy, Integrity, Perseverance, Self-Control and Indomitable Spirit

official.text: 1. Courtesy. 2. Integrity. 3. Perseverance. 4. Self-Control. 5. Indomitable Spirit.

items.simple: the tenets are the five big ideas every Taekwon-Do student tries to live by.
items.quiz: Can you name the five tenets of Taekwon-Do?
items.answer: Courtesy, Integrity, Perseverance, Self-Control and Indomitable Spirit.
wrong: Speed, power, kicking, punching and jumping.
Strength, balance, stretching, speed and winning.

items.title: Courtesy
items.simple: Courtesy is the first tenet. It means being polite and kind: saying please and thank you, bowing, listening to your instructor and being nice to other students.
items.learnBody: Courtesy is the first tenet. It means being polite and kind: saying please and thank you, bowing, listening to your instructor and being nice to other students.

items.title: Integrity
items.english: Being honest and doing the right thing
items.simple: Integrity is the second tenet. It means being honest, knowing what is right and wrong, and doing the right thing even when nobody is watching.
items.learnBody: Integrity is the second tenet. It means being honest, knowing what is right and wrong, and doing the right thing even when nobody is watching.
items.quiz: What does integrity mean?
items.answer: Being honest and doing the right thing.
wrong: Being the strongest in the class.

items.title: Perseverance
items.simple: Perseverance is the third tenet. It means you keep trying, even when something is hard, and you practise again and again until you get better.
items.learnBody: Perseverance is the third tenet. It means you keep trying, even when something is hard, and you practise again and again until you get better.

items.title: Self-Control
items.simple: Self-Control is the fourth tenet. It means you are the boss of your body and your feelings. You stay calm, you do not lose your temper, and you are careful not to hurt your partner.
items.learnBody: Self-Control is the fourth tenet. It means you are the boss of your body and your feelings. You stay calm, you do not lose your temper, and you are careful not to hurt your partner.

items.title: Indomitable Spirit
items.simple: Indomitable Spirit is the fifth tenet. It means being brave and having a strong heart: you stand up for what is right and you do not give up, even when you feel scared or tired.
items.learnBody: Indomitable Spirit is the fifth tenet. It means being brave and having a strong heart: you stand up for what is right and you do not give up, even when you feel scared or tired.

items.title: The student oath
items.english: I shall observe the Tenets of Taekwon-Do

official.text:
I shall observe the Tenets of Taekwon-Do
I shall respect the Instructor and Seniors.
I shall never misuse Taekwon-Do.
I shall be a champion of freedom and justice.
I shall build a more peaceful world.

items.simple: The first promise of the oath is "I shall observe the Tenets of Taekwon-Do". In simple words: I will follow the five tenets.
items.learnBody:
The student oath is five promises we say together in class.
Check with your instructor: some ITF groups use slightly different words (for example "help to build a more peaceful world"), so say it the way your club does.
items.quiz: What is the first line of the student oath?
items.answer: I shall observe the Tenets of Taekwon-Do
items.why: The first promise of the oath is "I shall observe the Tenets of Taekwon-Do". In simple words: I will follow the five tenets.

items.title: What the oath promises mean
items.english: Never use Taekwon-Do to hurt or bully anyone, only to stay safe
items.simple: In kid words: follow the five tenets, be respectful to your instructor and the older belts, never use Taekwon-Do to bully or show off, stand up for what is fair, and help make the world a kinder place.
items.learnBody: In kid words: follow the five tenets, be respectful to your instructor and the older belts, never use Taekwon-Do to bully or show off, stand up for what is fair, and help make the world a kinder place.
items.quiz: What does "I shall never misuse Taekwon-Do" mean?
items.answer: Never use Taekwon-Do to hurt or bully anyone, only to stay safe.
wrong: Never tell anyone you do Taekwon-Do.

items.title: Charyot (attention)
items.simple: Charyot means attention. When you hear charyot, you stand up straight in attention stance, quiet and still, ready to listen.
items.learnBody: Charyot means attention. When you hear charyot, you stand up straight in attention stance, quiet and still, ready to listen.
items.quiz: What does charyot mean?

items.title: Kyong ye (bow)
items.simple: Kyong ye means bow. We bow to show respect, for example to the instructor, to a partner, and when we come into or leave the training hall.
items.learnBody: Kyong ye means bow. We bow to show respect, for example to the instructor, to a partner, and when we come into or leave the training hall.
items.quiz: What does kyong ye mean?

items.title: Junbi (ready)
items.simple: Junbi means ready. When you hear junbi, you get into your ready stance and wait for the next command.
items.learnBody: Junbi means ready. When you hear junbi, you get into your ready stance and wait for the next command.
items.quiz: What does junbi mean?

items.title: Si jak (begin)
items.simple: Si jak means begin, or start. It is the command to start the exercise or the pattern.
items.learnBody: Si jak means begin, or start. It is the command to start the exercise or the pattern.
items.quiz: What does si jak mean?

items.title: Baro (return)
items.simple: Baro means return. When you hear baro at the end of an exercise, you go back to your ready position.
items.learnBody: Baro means return. When you hear baro at the end of an exercise, you go back to your ready position.
items.quiz: What does baro mean as a command?

items.title: Kihap (yell)
items.simple: Kihap means a yell or shout. A good kihap is short, loud and comes from your belly. It helps you breathe out and put power into a move.
items.learnBody: Kihap means a yell or shout. A good kihap is short, loud and comes from your belly. It helps you breathe out and put power into a move.
items.quiz: What is a kihap?

items.title: Dojang and dobok
items.simple: The dojang (do jang) is the training hall, the place where we practise. The dobok (do bok) is the white training uniform we wear.
items.learnBody: The dojang (do jang) is the training hall, the place where we practise. The dobok (do bok) is the white training uniform we wear.
items.quiz: What is a dobok?

items.title: Instructor (sabum nim)
items.simple: We call the instructor sabum nim. Some clubs use boosabum nim for a 1st to 3rd degree black belt instructor and sabum nim for 4th to 6th degree. Ask your club which one they use.
items.learnBody: We call the instructor sabum nim. Some clubs use boosabum nim for a 1st to 3rd degree black belt instructor and sabum nim for 4th to 6th degree. Ask your club which one they use.
items.quiz: What do we call the instructor in Korean?

items.title: High, middle and low
items.simple: Middle is kaunde, about shoulder level.
items.learnBody: Moves aim at three heights. High is nopunde (about eye level). Middle is kaunde (about shoulder level). Low is najunde (about belt level and below).
items.quiz: What is the Korean word for middle?
items.why: Middle is kaunde, about shoulder level.

items.title: Punch, block and kick words
items.simple: Three words you hear all the time: jirugi means punch, makgi means block, chagi means kick.
items.learnBody: Three words you hear all the time: jirugi means punch, makgi means block, chagi means kick.
items.quiz: What is the Korean word for block?

items.title: Attention stance (charyot sogi)
items.simple: Sogi means stance. Attention stance is charyot sogi. Stand tall with your heels together and your toes pointing out a little, like a V. Arms down by your sides, eyes looking forward.
items.learnBody: Sogi means stance. Attention stance is charyot sogi. Stand tall with your heels together and your toes pointing out a little, like a V. Arms down by your sides, eyes looking forward.
items.quiz: What is attention stance called in Korean?

items.title: Parallel stance and parallel ready stance
items.simple: Parallel stance is narani sogi. Your feet are about shoulder width apart and both point straight forward, like train tracks. Parallel ready stance is narani junbi sogi: the same feet, with both fists held in front of your belt. Chon-Ji and Saju Jirugi start from parallel ready stance.
aliases: parallel stance and parallel ready stance
items.learnBody: Parallel stance is narani sogi. Your feet are about shoulder width apart and both point straight forward, like train tracks. Parallel ready stance is narani junbi sogi: the same feet, with both fists held in front of your belt. Chon-Ji and Saju Jirugi start from parallel ready stance.
items.quiz: What is parallel ready stance called in Korean?

items.title: Walking stance (gunnun sogi)
items.simple: Walking stance is gunnun sogi. One foot is in front, like taking a big step. Bend your front knee, keep your back leg straight, and keep your weight even on both feet. If your left foot is in front it is a left walking stance.
items.learnBody: Walking stance is gunnun sogi. One foot is in front, like taking a big step. Bend your front knee, keep your back leg straight, and keep your weight even on both feet. If your left foot is in front it is a left walking stance.
items.quiz: What is walking stance called in Korean?

items.title: Stepping forward and backward
items.simple: Nagagi means stepping forward. Duruogi means stepping backward. We practise stepping in walking stance before we learn patterns.
items.learnBody: Nagagi means stepping forward. Duruogi means stepping backward. We practise stepping in walking stance before we learn patterns.
items.quiz: What is the Korean word for stepping forward?

items.title: Forearm low block (palmok najunde makgi)
items.simple: A forearm low block is palmok najunde makgi. Palmok means forearm. You sweep your forearm down and out to stop a kick or punch aimed at your tummy or legs. It is the first move of Chon-Ji.
items.learnBody: A forearm low block is palmok najunde makgi. Palmok means forearm. You sweep your forearm down and out to stop a kick or punch aimed at your tummy or legs. It is the first move of Chon-Ji.
items.quiz: What is a forearm low block called in Korean?

items.title: Knife-hand low block (sonkal najunde makgi)
items.simple: A knife-hand low block is sonkal najunde makgi. Sonkal means knife-hand: an open hand with the fingers together, blocking with the little-finger edge. It is a low block, used in Saju Makgi.
items.learnBody: A knife-hand low block is sonkal najunde makgi. Sonkal means knife-hand: an open hand with the fingers together, blocking with the little-finger edge. It is a low block, used in Saju Makgi.
items.quiz: What is a knife-hand low block called in Korean?

items.title: Inner forearm side block (an palmok yop makgi)
items.simple: An inner forearm side block is an palmok yop makgi. An palmok means inner forearm, the thumb side of your arm. You bring it across to block at middle height. It is used in Saju Makgi and in Chon-Ji.
aliases: inner forearm side block (an palmok yop makgi)
items.learnBody: An inner forearm side block is an palmok yop makgi. An palmok means inner forearm, the thumb side of your arm. You bring it across to block at middle height. It is used in Saju Makgi and in Chon-Ji.
items.quiz: What is an inner forearm side block called in Korean?

items.title: Front punch (ap jirugi)
items.simple: A front punch is ap jirugi. You punch with the forefist (ap joomuk): the first two big knuckles of your fist. You can punch high (nopunde), middle (kaunde) or low (najunde). The other hand pulls back to your hip.
items.learnBody: A front punch is ap jirugi. You punch with the forefist (ap joomuk): the first two big knuckles of your fist. You can punch high (nopunde), middle (kaunde) or low (najunde). The other hand pulls back to your hip.
items.quiz: What part of the hand do you punch with in a front punch?
items.answer: The forefist, the first two big knuckles.
wrong: The little finger side of the fist.

items.title: Front snap kick (apcha busigi)
items.simple: A front snap kick is apcha busigi. Lift your knee, snap your foot out and pull it straight back. You hit with the ball of your foot (ap kumchi), so pull your toes back.
items.learnBody: A front snap kick is apcha busigi. Lift your knee, snap your foot out and pull it straight back. You hit with the ball of your foot (ap kumchi), so pull your toes back.
items.quiz: Which part of the foot do you use for a front snap kick?

items.title: Front rising kick (apcha olligi)
items.simple: A front rising kick is apcha olligi. Keep your kicking leg straight and swing it up in front of you, then bring it back down with control. It helps stretch your legs.
items.learnBody: A front rising kick is apcha olligi. Keep your kicking leg straight and swing it up in front of you, then bring it back down with control. It helps stretch your legs.
items.quiz: What is a front rising kick called in Korean?

items.title: Saju Jirugi (four-direction punch)
items.simple: Saju means four directions and jirugi means punch, so Saju Jirugi is the four-direction punch. It is a practice exercise, not a pattern. You start in parallel ready stance, punch in walking stance, then turn with a low block and punch again, until you have faced all four directions. You do it once starting with the right foot and once with the left.
items.learnBody: Saju means four directions and jirugi means punch, so Saju Jirugi is the four-direction punch. It is a practice exercise, not a pattern. You start in parallel ready stance, punch in walking stance, then turn with a low block and punch again, until you have faced all four directions. You do it once starting with the right foot and once with the left.
items.quiz: What does Saju Jirugi mean?

items.title: Saju Makgi (four-direction block)
items.simple: Saju Makgi is the four-direction block. It is also a practice exercise. In walking stance you do a knife-hand low block, then step forward with an inner forearm middle block, and you turn so you block in all four directions. You do it once on each side.
items.learnBody: Saju Makgi is the four-direction block. It is also a practice exercise. In walking stance you do a knife-hand low block, then step forward with an inner forearm middle block, and you turn so you block in all four directions. You do it once on each side.
items.quiz: What does Saju Makgi mean?

items.title: What a pattern (tul) is
items.simple: A pattern is called tul (you may also see it spelled teul). It is a set of moves done in a fixed order, as if fighting pretend opponents. ITF Taekwon-Do has 24 patterns. Chon-Ji is the first one.
items.learnBody: A pattern is called tul (you may also see it spelled teul). It is a set of moves done in a fixed order, as if fighting pretend opponents. ITF Taekwon-Do has 24 patterns. Chon-Ji is the first one.
items.quiz: What is the Korean word for pattern?

items.title: What Chon-Ji means

official.text: Chon-Ji means literally “the Heaven the Earth”. It is, in the Orient, interpreted as the creation of the world or the beginning of human history, therefore, it is the initial pattern played by the beginner. This pattern consists of two similar parts; one to represent the Heaven and the other the Earth.

items.simple: Chon is Heaven (the sky above) and Ji is Earth (the ground below). It is about how everything began, so it is the first pattern you learn. It has two halves that are alike: one for Heaven and one for Earth.
items.quiz: What does Chon-Ji mean?
items.why: Chon-Ji means literally "the Heaven the Earth". In simple words: it is the first pattern, about how everything began.

items.title: How many moves Chon-Ji has
items.simple: Chon-Ji has 19 moves. It is the pattern you need for the grading from 9th kup to 8th kup (yellow stripe to yellow belt).
items.learnBody: Chon-Ji has 19 moves. It is the pattern you need for the grading from 9th kup to 8th kup (yellow stripe to yellow belt).
items.quiz: How many moves are in Chon-Ji?

items.title: Chon-Ji start position and diagram
items.simple: Chon-Ji starts in parallel ready stance (narani junbi sogi). The floor pattern is a cross, like a plus sign. You stand in the middle facing D (the front). A is to your right, B is to your left and C is behind you.
items.learnBody: Chon-Ji starts in parallel ready stance (narani junbi sogi). The floor pattern is a cross, like a plus sign. You stand in the middle facing D (the front). A is to your right, B is to your left and C is behind you.
items.quiz: Which stance does Chon-Ji start in?

items.title: Chon-Ji moves 1 to 4
items.english: Left walking stance to the left with a left forearm low block
items.simple: Moves 1 to 4:
items.learnBody:
Moves 1 to 4:
1. Step the left foot to the left (B) into a left walking stance and do a low block with the left forearm.
2. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
3. Turn to the right (clockwise) towards A, into a right walking stance, and do a low block with the right forearm.
4. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
items.quiz: What is the very first move of Chon-Ji?
items.answer: Left walking stance to the left with a left forearm low block.
wrong: Right walking stance to the right with a right forearm low block.
Sitting stance with a middle punch.

moves.text: Step the left foot to the left (B) into a left walking stance and do a low block with the left forearm.
Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
Turn to the right (clockwise) towards A, into a right walking stance, and do a low block with the right forearm.
Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.

items.title: Chon-Ji moves 5 to 8
items.english: A forearm low block in walking stance
items.simple: Moves 5 to 8:
items.learnBody:
Moves 5 to 8:
5. Turn to face the front (D) with the left foot, into a left walking stance, and do a low block with the left forearm.
6. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
7. Turn to the right (clockwise) to face the back (C), into a right walking stance, and do a low block with the right forearm.
8. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
That is the end of the first part, the part for Heaven.
items.quiz: In Chon-Ji, which block do you do in moves 5 and 7?
items.answer: A forearm low block in walking stance.
wrong: A knife-hand low block in sitting stance.
An inner forearm block in L-stance.

moves.text: Turn to face the front (D) with the left foot, into a left walking stance, and do a low block with the left forearm.
Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
Turn to the right (clockwise) to face the back (C), into a right walking stance, and do a low block with the right forearm.
Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.

items.title: Chon-Ji moves 9 to 12
items.simple: The second part, the part for Earth, uses L-stance for the blocks.
items.learnBody:
The second part, the part for Earth, uses L-stance for the blocks.
9. Move the left foot towards A into a right L-stance and do a middle block with the left inner forearm.
10. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
11. Turn clockwise towards B into a left L-stance and do a middle block with the right inner forearm.
12. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
items.quiz: Which stance do you use for the block in Chon-Ji move 9?

moves.text: Move the left foot towards A into a right L-stance and do a middle block with the left inner forearm.
Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
Turn clockwise towards B into a left L-stance and do a middle block with the right inner forearm.
Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.

items.title: Chon-Ji moves 13 to 16
items.simple: In move 13 you block with the left inner forearm, and in move 15 with the right inner forearm.
items.learnBody:
13. Move the left foot towards C into a right L-stance and do a middle block with the left inner forearm.
14. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
15. Turn clockwise towards D into a left L-stance and do a middle block with the right inner forearm.
16. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
items.quiz: In Chon-Ji moves 13 and 15, which part of the arm blocks?
items.why: In move 13 you block with the left inner forearm, and in move 15 with the right inner forearm.

moves.text: Move the left foot towards C into a right L-stance and do a middle block with the left inner forearm.
Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
Turn clockwise towards D into a left L-stance and do a middle block with the right inner forearm.
Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.

items.title: Chon-Ji moves 17 to 19 and the end
items.english: Bring the left foot back to the ready position
items.simple: At the end, bring the left foot back to parallel ready stance.
aliases: chon-ji moves 17 to 19 and the end
items.learnBody:
17. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
18. Step backwards with the right foot into a left walking stance, still facing D, and do a middle punch with the left fist.
19. Step backwards with the left foot into a right walking stance, still facing D, and do a middle punch with the right fist.
End: bring the left foot back to parallel ready stance.
items.quiz: How does Chon-Ji end?
items.answer: Bring the left foot back to the ready position.
wrong: With a spin on the spot.
items.why: At the end, bring the left foot back to parallel ready stance.

moves.text: Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
Step backwards with the right foot into a left walking stance, still facing D, and do a middle punch with the left fist.
Step backwards with the left foot into a right walking stance, still facing D, and do a middle punch with the right fist.

items.end: bring the left foot back to parallel ready stance.

items.title: Punches in Chon-Ji (obverse punch)
items.english: The hand on the same side as the front foot
items.simple: All the punches in Chon-Ji are middle obverse punches (kaunde baro jirugi). Obverse means you punch with the hand on the same side as your front foot: right foot in front, right fist punches. A reverse punch (bandae jirugi) uses the other hand.
items.learnBody: All the punches in Chon-Ji are middle obverse punches (kaunde baro jirugi). Obverse means you punch with the hand on the same side as your front foot: right foot in front, right fist punches. A reverse punch (bandae jirugi) uses the other hand.
items.quiz: In an obverse punch, which hand punches?
items.answer: The hand on the same side as the front foot.
wrong: The hand on the other side from the front foot.
Both hands at the same time.

items.title: L-stance (niunja sogi)
items.simple: L-stance is niunja sogi. Your feet make a shape like the letter L. Most of your weight is on your back leg and both knees are bent. If your right leg is at the back it is called a right L-stance. Chon-Ji uses L-stance for the inner forearm blocks.
items.learnBody: L-stance is niunja sogi. Your feet make a shape like the letter L. Most of your weight is on your back leg and both knees are bent. If your right leg is at the back it is called a right L-stance. Chon-Ji uses L-stance for the inner forearm blocks.
items.quiz: What is L-stance called in Korean?

items.title: Sitting stance (annun sogi)
items.simple: Sitting stance is annun sogi. Your feet are wide apart and point forward, your knees bend out over your feet, and your back stays straight, like sitting on a horse. Your weight is even on both feet.
items.learnBody: Sitting stance is annun sogi. Your feet are wide apart and point forward, your knees bend out over your feet, and your back stays straight, like sitting on a horse. Your weight is even on both feet.
items.quiz: What is sitting stance called in Korean?

items.title: What the yellow belt means
items.english: The earth from which a plant sprouts and takes root as the Taekwon-Do foundation is being laid

official.text: Yellow signifies the earth from which a plant sprouts and takes root as the Taekwon-Do foundation is being laid.

items.simple: yellow is the colour of the earth. Like a seed putting down roots before it grows tall, at yellow belt you practise the basics until they are strong.
items.quiz: What does the yellow belt mean?
items.answer: The earth from which a plant sprouts and takes root as the Taekwon-Do foundation is being laid.
wrong: The Heaven, towards which the plant matures into a towering tree as training in Taekwon-Do progresses.
Danger, cautioning the student to exercise control and warning the opponent to stay away.
items.why: In simple words: yellow is the earth. Like a seed putting down roots, you are building strong basics.

items.title: Belt order for the first gradings
items.english: White belt with a yellow stripe (9th kup)
items.simple: 10th kup is white belt. 9th kup is white belt with a yellow stripe (some clubs call it a tag).
aliases: belt order for the first gradings
items.learnBody: Coloured belt grades are called kup (also spelled gup) and they count down. 10th kup is white belt. After white belt comes a white belt with a yellow stripe (9th kup; some clubs call it a tag). 8th kup is yellow belt.
items.quiz: Which belt comes after white belt?
items.answer: White belt with a yellow stripe (9th kup).
wrong: Yellow belt with a green stripe.
items.why: 10th kup is white belt. 9th kup is white belt with a yellow stripe (some clubs call it a tag).

items.title: Turning in place and step turning
items.simple: Dolgi means turning. Spot turning (gujari dolgi) means you turn around where you are standing. Step turning means you take a step as you turn. Chon-Ji has turns, so practise turning without losing your balance.
aliases: turning in place and step turning

items.title: Counting 1 to 10 in Korean
items.english: Counting from one to ten in Korean
items.simple: 1 hana, 2 dul, 3 set, 4 net, 5 dasot, 6 yosot, 7 ilgop, 8 yodul, 9 ahop, 10 yol. (Dul is sometimes spelled dool.)
items.learnBody: 1 hana, 2 dul, 3 set, 4 net, 5 dasot, 6 yosot, 7 ilgop, 8 yodul, 9 ahop, 10 yol. (Dul is sometimes spelled dool.)
items.quiz: How do you count to ten in Korean?
items.answer: Hana, dul, set, net, dasot, yosot, ilgop, yodul, ahop, yol.
wrong: Yosot, ilgop, yodul, ahop, yol, hana, dul, set, net, dasot.
Hana, set, dul, dasot, net, yosot, yodul, ilgop, ahop, yol.
items.why: 1 hana, 2 dul, 3 set, 4 net, 5 dasot, 6 yosot, 7 ilgop, 8 yodul, 9 ahop, 10 yol.
